{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
----
# How to contribute to Fizzy

Fizzy uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are

# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.

# How to contribute to Fizzy

Fizzy uses GitHub

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

## Development

### Setting up

First, get everything installed and configured with:

```sh
bin/setup
bin/setup --reset # Reset the database and seed it
```

And then run the development server:

```sh
bin/dev
```

You'll be able to access the app in development at http://app.fizzy.localhost:3006.

To log in, enter `david@example.com`. In development the verification code is shown on the page itself, under "Psst, here's your code" — no need to check your email.

### Web Push Notifications

Fizzy uses VAPID (Voluntary Application Server Identification) keys to send browser push notifications. For notifications to work in development you'll need to generate a key pair and set these environment variables:

- `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`

Generate them with the `web-push` gem:

```ruby

puts "VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=#{vapid_key.private_key}"
puts "VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=#{vapid_key.public_key}"
```

### Running tests

For fast feedback loops, unit tests can be run with:

```sh
bin/rails test
```

The full continuous integration tests can be run with:

```sh
bin/ci
```

### Database configuration

Fizzy works with SQLite by default and supports MySQL too. You can switch adapters with the `DATABASE_ADAPTER` environment variable. For example, to develop locally against MySQL:

```sh
DATABASE_ADAPTER=mysql bin/setup --reset
DATABASE_ADAPTER=mysql bin/ci
```

The remote CI pipeline will run tests against both SQLite and MySQL.

### Outbound Emails

You can view email previews at http://app.fizzy.localhost:3006/rails/mailers.

You can enable or disable [`letter_opener`](https://github.com/ryanb/letter_opener) to open sent emails automatically with:

```sh

```

Under the hood, this will create or remove `tmp/email-dev.txt`.

This gem depends on some private git repositories and it is not meant to be used by third parties. But we hope it can serve as inspiration for anyone wanting to run fizzy on their own infrastructure.

"

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/work && cat > /tmp/work/inventory.rb <<'EOF'
# usage: ruby inventory.rb path/to/schema.rb
path = ARGV[0]
tables = {}
cur = nil
File.readlines(path).each do |line|
  if (m = line.match(/^\s*create_table "([^"]+)"/))
    cur = m[1]
    tables[cur] = { cols: {}, idx: [] }
  elsif cur && line =~ /^\s*end\s*$/
    cur = nil
  elsif cur && (m = line.match(/^\s*t\.(\w+) "([^"]+)"(.*)/)) && m[1] != "index"
    tables[cur][:cols][m[2]] = [m[1], m[3]]
  elsif cur && (m = line.match(/^\s*t\.index \[(.*?)\]/))
    tables[cur][:idx] << m[1]
  end
end
puts "tables: #{tables.size}"
tables.sort.each do |t, v|
  acc = v[:cols]["account_id"]
  if acc
    nullable = !acc[1].include?("null: false")
    lead = v[:idx].any? { |i| i.start_with?('"account_id"') }
    any = v[:idx].any? { |i| i.include?('"account_id"') }
    flag = "account_id #{nullable ? 'NULLABLE' : 'NOT NULL'} #{lead ? 'indexed(lead)' : (any ? 'indexed(non-lead)' : 'NO-INDEX')}"
  else
    flag = "-- NO account_id"
  end
  puts format("%-34s %s", t, flag)
end
EOF
cd /app && ruby /tmp/work/inventory.rb db/schema.rb

class Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  class IntegrityError < StandardError; end
  class ConflictError < IntegrityError; end

  IMPORT_BATCH_SIZE = 100
  INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES = %w[Export Account::Import].freeze

  attr_accessor :importable_model_names
  attr_reader :account, :model, :attributes

  def initialize(account:, model:, attributes: nil, importable_model_names: nil)
    @account = account
    @model = model
    @attributes = (attributes || model.column_names).map(&:to_s)
    @importable_model_names = importable_model_names || [ model.name ]
  end

  def export(to:, start: nil)
    with_zip(to) do
      block = lambda do |record|
        export_record(record)
      end

      records.respond_to?(:find_each) ? records.find_each(&block) : records.each(&block)
    end
  end

  def import(from:, start: nil, callback: nil)
    with_zip(from) do
      file_list = files
      file_list = skip_to(file_list, start) if start

      file_list.each_slice(IMPORT_BATCH_SIZE) do |file_batch|
        import_batch(file_batch)
        callback&.call(record_set: self, files: file_batch)
      end
    end
  end

  def check(from:, start: nil, callback: nil)
    with_zip(from) do
      file_list = files
      file_list = skip_to(file_list, start) if start

      file_list.each do |file_path|
        check_record(file_path)
        callback&.call(record_set: self, file: file_path)
      end
    end
  end

  private
    attr_reader :zip

    def with_zip(zip)
      old_zip = @zip
      @zip = zip
      yield
    ensure
      @zip = old_zip
    end

    def records
      model.where(account_id: account.id)
    end

    def export_record(record)
      zip.add_file "data/#{model_dir}/#{record.id}.json", record.attributes.slice(*attributes).to_json
    end

    def files
      zip.glob("data/#{model_dir}/*.json")
    end

    def import_batch(files)
      batch_data = files.map do |file|
        data = load(file)
        data.slice(*attributes).merge("account_id" => account.id).tap do |record_data|
          record_data["updated_at"] = Time.current if record_data.key?("updated_at")
        end
      end

      model.insert_all!(batch_data)
    end

    def check_record(file_path)
      data = load(file_path)
      expected_id = File.basename(file_path, ".json")

      unless data["id"].to_s == expected_id
        raise IntegrityError, "#{model} record ID mismatch: expected #{expected_id}, got #{data['id']}"
      end

      missing = attributes - data.keys
      if missing.any?
        raise IntegrityError, "#{file_path} is missing required fields: #{missing.join(', ')}"
      end

      if model.exists?(id: data["id"])
        raise ConflictError, "#{model} record with ID #{data['id']} already exists"
      end

      check_associations_dont_exist(data)
    end

    def check_associations_dont_exist(data)
      model.reflect_on_all_associations(:belongs_to).each do |association|
        foreign_key = association.foreign_key.to_s

        if associated_id = data[foreign_key]
          check_association_doesnt_exist(data, association, associated_id)
        end
      end
    end

    def check_association_doesnt_exist(data, association, associated_id)
      if association.polymorphic?
        type_column = association.foreign_type.to_s
        associated_class = verify_model_type(data[type_column])
      else
        associated_class = association.klass
      end

      if associated_class.exists?(id: associated_id)
        raise ConflictError, "#{model} record references existing #{association.name} (#{associated_class}) with ID #{associated_id}"
      end
    end

    def verify_model_type(type_name)
      if importable_model_names.include?(type_name)
        type_name.constantize
      else
        raise IntegrityError, "Unrecognized model type: #{type_name}"
      end
    end

    def skip_to(file_list, last_id)
      index = file_list.index(last_id)

      if index
        file_list[(index + 1)..]
      else
        file_list
      end
    end

    def load(file_path)
      JSON.parse(zip.read(file_path))
    rescue ArgumentError => e
      raise IntegrityError, e.message
    end

    def model_dir
      model.table_name
    end
end

# Enforce storage ledger integrity by preventing blob reuse in tracked contexts.
#
# Two invariants:
# 1. Account match: blob.account_id == record.account_id (multi-tenant safety)
# 2. No reuse within tracked contexts: a blob can only have one tracked attachment
#
# With per-attachment reconcile, blob reuse inside an account wouldn't break correctness -
# ledger would still count each attach, and reconcile would agree. However, we intentionally
# forbid reuse (except templates) as a product/control decision:
# - Simpler mental model (one blob = one attachment)
# - Prevents accidental quota manipulation via direct blob_id reuse
# - Cleaner audit trail in ledger entries
#
# Scope note: The no-reuse validation only blocks reuse when the *new* attachment is tracked
# AND only checks *existing* attachments in Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES. A blob first
# attached to an untracked type (avatar/export) could theoretically be reused in a tracked
# context. This is acceptable - user-accessible blob IDs from untracked contexts are
# basically nonexistent in practice.
#
# Exception: ActionText embeds are allowed to reuse blobs to support copy/paste.

ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_storage_attachment) do
  validate :blob_account_matches_record, on: :create
  validate :no_tracked_blob_reuse, on: :create

  private
    # Multi-tenant safety: blob must belong to same account as record
    # NOTE: Skips validation if record.account is nil. This is a theoretical bypass
    # if someone attaches before account assignment, but our flows assign account
    # before attachment. Global/unaccounted attachments (Identity/User avatars, exports)
    # bypass tenancy checks via try(:account) returning nil - this is intentional as
    # these classes don't participate in storage tracking.
    def blob_account_matches_record
      if record&.try(:account).present? && !whitelisted_for_cross_account?
        unless blob&.account_id == record.account.id
          errors.add(:blob_id, "blob account must match record account")
        end
      end
    end

    # Ledger integrity: blob can only have one tracked attachment
    def no_tracked_blob_reuse
      tracked_record = record&.try(:storage_tracked_record)
      if tracked_record.present? &&
          !whitelisted_for_cross_account? &&
          !(record_type == "ActionText::RichText" && name == "embeds")

        # Check for existing attachment of this blob in tracked contexts
        # Uses Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES constant to stay generic
        existing = ActiveStorage::Attachment
          .where(blob_id: blob_id)
          .where(record_type: Storage::TRACKED_RECORD_TYPES)
          .where.not(id: id)
          .exists?

        if existing
          errors.add(:blob_id, "cannot reuse blob in tracked storage context")
        end
      end
    end

    def whitelisted_for_cross_account?
      # Only template account blobs can be reused cross-tenant.
      # When TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID is nil, no exemptions are granted.
      Storage::TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID.present? && blob&.account_id == Storage::TEMPLATE_ACCOUNT_ID
    end
end

# Fizzy-specific override: ActiveStorage's default purge path uses `delete`,
# which skips attachment callbacks. We need `destroy` so storage ledger detaches
# are recorded and reused blobs (ActionText embeds) aren't purged until the
# last attachment is gone. Keep this local to Fizzy; it's not a Rails default.
module ActiveStorage
  module PurgeOnLastAttachment
    def purge
      @purge_mode = :purge
      destroy
      purge_blob_if_last(:purge) if destroyed?
    ensure
      @purge_mode = nil
    end

    def purge_later
      @purge_mode = :purge_later
      destroy
      purge_blob_if_last(:purge_later) if destroyed?
    ensure
      @purge_mode = nil
    end

    private
      # Rails registers `after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob` (renamed from
      # `purge_dependent_blob_later` upstream, which also now handles dependent: :purge).
      # Override the current callback name so reused blobs (ActionText embeds) are only
      # purged once the last attachment is gone, and skip when an explicit purge/purge_later
      # is already driving the blob purge via `purge_blob_if_last` (@purge_mode set).
      def purge_dependent_blob
        return if @purge_mode

        # `record.nil?` must be checked first: `dependent` reads `record.attachment_reflections`,
        # so it can't be evaluated for an orphaned attachment — an absent record falls back to
        # purge_later.
        if record.nil? || dependent == :purge_later
          purge_blob_if_last(:purge_later)
        elsif dependent == :purge
          purge_blob_if_last(:purge)
        end
      end

      def purge_blob_if_last(mode)
        if blob && !blob.attachments.exists?
          mode == :purge ? blob.purge : blob.purge_later
        end
      end
  end
end

  prepend ActiveStorage::PurgeOnLastAttachment
end

      if uuid_primary_key?
        pending_attribute_modifications << PendingUuidDefault.new(primary_key)
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid
      # Table doesn't exist yet
    end

    def uuid_primary_key?
      table_name && primary_key && schema_cache.columns_hash(table_name)[primary_key]&.type == :uuid
    end

    PendingUuidDefault = Struct.new(:name) do
      def apply_to(attribute_set)
        attribute_set[name] = attribute_set[name].with_user_default(-> { ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate })
      end
    end

class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  broadcasts_refreshes

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :identity

  has_one_attached :file, dependent: :purge_later

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending
  enum :failure_reason, %w[ conflict invalid_export ].index_by(&:itself), prefix: :failed_due_to, scopes: false

  scope :expired, -> { where(completed_at: ...24.hours.ago).or(where(status: :failed, created_at: ...7.days.ago)) }

  def self.cleanup
    expired.each(&:cleanup)
  end

  def process_later
    Account::DataImportJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def check(start: nil, callback: nil)
    processing!

    ZipFile.read_from(file.blob) do |zip|
      Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(account).each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, last_id|
        record_set.check(from: zip, start: last_id, callback: callback)
      end
    end
  rescue Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::ConflictError => e
    mark_as_failed(:conflict)
    raise e
  rescue Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::IntegrityError, ZipFile::InvalidFileError => e
    mark_as_failed(:invalid_export)
    raise e
  rescue => e
    mark_as_failed
    raise e
  end

  def process(start: nil, callback: nil)
    processing!

    ZipFile.read_from(file.blob) do |zip|
      Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(account).each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, last_id|
        record_set.import(from: zip, start: last_id, callback: callback)
      end
    end

    add_importer_to_all_access_boards
    reconcile_cards_count
    reconcile_account_storage

    mark_completed
  rescue Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::ConflictError => e
    mark_as_failed(:conflict)
    raise e
  rescue Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet::IntegrityError, ZipFile::InvalidFileError => e
    mark_as_failed(:invalid_export)
    raise e
  rescue => e
    mark_as_failed
    raise e
  end

  def cleanup
    destroy
    account.destroy if failed?
  end

  private
    def mark_completed
      update!(status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current)
      ImportMailer.completed(identity, account).deliver_later
    end

    def mark_as_failed(failure_reason = nil)
      update!(status: :failed, failure_reason: failure_reason)
      ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
    end

    def reconcile_cards_count
      account.update_column :cards_count, [ account.cards_count, account.cards.maximum(:number).to_i ].max
    end

    def add_importer_to_all_access_boards
      importer = account.users.find_by!(identity: identity)

      account.boards.all_access.find_each do |board|
        board.accesses.grant_to(importer)
      end
    end

    def reconcile_account_storage
      account.boards.each(&:reconcile_storage)
      account.reconcile_storage
      account.materialize_storage
    end
end

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  INDEXES = %w[ all closed not_now stalled postponing_soon golden ]
  SORTED_BY = %w[ newest oldest latest ]

  delegate :default_value?, to: :class

  class_methods do
    def default_values
      { indexed_by: "all", sorted_by: "latest" }
    end

    def default_value?(key, value)
      default_values[key.to_sym].eql?(value)
    end

    def indexed_by_human_name(index)
      case index
      when "postponing_soon"
        "Closing soon"
      when "closed"
        "Done"
      when "all"
        "Open"
      else
        index.humanize
      end
    end
  end

  included do
    store_accessor :fields, :assignment_status, :indexed_by, :sorted_by, :terms,
      :card_ids, :creation, :closure, :column_ids

    def assignment_status
      super.to_s.inquiry
    end

    def indexed_by
      (super || default_indexed_by).inquiry
    end

    def sorted_by
      (super || default_sorted_by).inquiry
    end

    def creation_window
      TimeWindowParser.parse(creation)
    end

    def closure_window
      TimeWindowParser.parse(closure)
    end

    def terms
      Array(super)
    end

    def terms=(value)
      super(Array(value).filter(&:present?))
    end

    def column_ids
      Array(super).filter(&:present?).uniq
    end

    def column_ids=(value)
      super(Array(value).filter(&:present?).uniq)
    end
  end

  def with(**fields)
    creator.filters.from_params(as_params).tap do |filter|
      fields.each do |key, value|
        filter.public_send("#{key}=", value)
      end
    end
  end

  def default_indexed_by
    self.class.default_values[:indexed_by]
  end

  def default_indexed_by?
    default_value?(:indexed_by, indexed_by)
  end

  def default_sorted_by
    self.class.default_values[:sorted_by]
  end

  def default_sorted_by?
    default_value?(:sorted_by, sorted_by)
  end
end

class Storage::Entry < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :board, optional: true
  belongs_to :recordable, polymorphic: true, optional: true

  scope :pending, ->(last_entry_id) { where.not(id: ..last_entry_id) if last_entry_id }

  thread_mattr_accessor :recording, default: true

  def self.suppressing_recording(&block)
    original, self.recording = self.recording, false
    yield
  ensure
    self.recording = original
  end

  # Records may be destroyed (during cascading deletes) but .id still works.
  # Skip entirely if account is destroyed - no need to track storage for deleted accounts.
  # Skip materialize jobs for destroyed boards since there's nothing to update.
  def self.record(delta:, operation:, account:, board: nil, recordable: nil, blob: nil)
    return if delta.zero?
    return if account.destroyed?
    return unless recording

    board&.materialize_storage_later unless board&.destroyed?

  end

  "output": "module Board::Accessible
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :delete_all do
      def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
        transaction do
          grant_to granted
          revoke_from revoked
        end
      end

      def grant_to(users)
        Access.insert_all Array(users).collect { |user| { id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate, board_id: proxy_association.owner.id, user_id: user.id } }
      end

      def revoke_from(users)
        destroy_by user: users unless proxy_association.owner.all_access?
      end
    end

    has_many :users, through: :accesses
    has_many :access_only_users, -> { merge(Access.access_only) }, through: :accesses, source: :user

    scope :all_access, -> { where(all_access: true) }

    after_create :grant_access_to_creator
    after_save_commit :grant_access_to_everyone
  end

  def accessed_by(user)
    access_for(user).accessed
  end

  def access_for(user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def accessible_to?(user)
    access_for(user).present?
  end

  def clean_inaccessible_data_for(user)
    return if accessible_to?(user)

    mentions_for_user(user).destroy_all
    notifications_for_user(user).destroy_all
    watches_for(user).destroy_all
    pins_for(user).destroy_all
  end

  def watchers
    users.active.where(accesses: { involvement: :watching })
  end

# Fix for SQLite FTS5 virtual table schema dumping
# Rails has a bug where it doesn't handle FTS5 content= and content_rowid= options

module SQLiteFTS5SchemaDumperFix
  # Override the virtual_tables method to handle FTS5 syntax properly
  def virtual_tables(stream)
    # Query sqlite_master for all virtual tables
    virtual_table_sqls = @connection.select_rows(
      "SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND sql LIKE 'CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE%'"
    )

    virtual_table_sqls.each do |table_name, sql|
      # Just output the raw SQL since create_virtual_table doesn't handle our syntax
      stream.puts "  execute #{sql.inspect}"
      stream.puts
    end
  end
end

messages.content:
The filter tests write `assignees`, `tags`, and `boards` through the association, so a has-many-through rewrite must keep those writers working.

I have enough to commit to a design. Here's the plan:

1. **One data migration** that adds `account_id` where it's missing, backfills it from each row's parent chain in parent-first order, deletes orphans (no resolvable account, or a required reference that no longer exists), then sets NOT NULL and an index. Blobs take their account from attachments.
2. **Models** get `belongs_to :account, default: -> { parent.account }`, following the existing core-model pattern. `Search::Query` gets its `user` association, `Webhook::Delivery` gets `account`, and the incinerate bug gets fixed.
3. **Filter habtm joins** become explicit join models, because `insert_all`-style habtm rows can't take a default.
4. **Insert paths** that bypass callbacks (`Access.insert_all`) pass `account_id` explicitly.
5. **Fixtures and schema dumps** get updated to match.

I'll start with a snapshot of the current state so I can diff later, then write the migration.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > db/migrate/20260710120000_require_account_id_on_tenant_tables.rb <<'EOF'
# Finishes the multi-tenant rollout. account_id was only ever added to the core tables,
# so every other table that holds an account's data gets one here, backfilled from the
# row's parent, made required, and indexed.
#
# A row is an orphan when its account can't be resolved through its parent chain, or when
# a required reference points at a row that no longer exists. Orphans are deleted. Blobs
# take their account from their attachments, so unattached blobs are deleted as well.
# Only rows are removed: files already stored for deleted blobs are left in the service.
class RequireAccountIdOnTenantTables < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.2]
  # Tables that already had an account_id column before this migration.
  PRE_EXISTING = %w[
    account_imports account_join_codes boards cards columns comments events filters
    notification_bundles notifications push_subscriptions steps tags users webhooks
  ].freeze

  def up
    tenant_tables.each do |table, owner, requires|
      add_reference table, :account, type: :uuid, null: true, index: false unless column_exists?(table, :account_id)
      execute "UPDATE #{table} SET account_id = #{owner} WHERE account_id IS NULL" if owner
      execute prune_sql(table, requires)
      change_column_null table, :account_id, false
      add_index table, :account_id unless leading_account_index?(table)
    end
  end

  def down
    tenant_tables.reverse_each do |table, _owner, _requires|
      if PRE_EXISTING.include?(table)
        change_column_null table, :account_id, true
        remove_index table, :account_id if index_exists?(table, :account_id) && table != "account_imports"
      else
        remove_column table, :account_id
      end
    end
  end

  private
    # Returns [table, owner SQL, required references] in the order tables must be processed.
    # A parent is backfilled and pruned before any of its children, so a child whose parent
    # was dropped resolves to no account and is dropped too.
    def tenant_tables
      [
        [ "users", nil, [] ],
        [ "tags", nil, [] ],
        [ "account_join_codes", nil, [] ],
        [ "account_imports", nil, [ %w[ identity_id identities ] ] ],

        [ "boards", owned_by("boards", "users", "creator_id"), [ %w[ creator_id users ] ] ],
        [ "filters", owned_by("filters", "users", "creator_id"), [ %w[ creator_id users ] ] ],
        [ "columns", owned_by("columns", "boards", "board_id"), [ %w[ board_id boards ] ] ],
        [ "cards", owned_by("cards", "boards", "board_id"), [ %w[ board_id boards ], %w[ creator_id users ] ] ],
        [ "events", owned_by("events", "boards", "board_id"), [ %w[ board_id boards ], %w[ creator_id users ] ] ],
        [ "webhooks", owned_by("webhooks", "boards", "board_id"), [ %w[ board_id boards ] ] ],

        [ "entropies", owned_by_polymorphic("entropies", "container", ACCOUNT_OR_BOARD), [] ],
        [ "storage_totals", owned_by_polymorphic("storage_totals", "owner", ACCOUNT_OR_BOARD), [] ],
        [ "board_publications", owned_by("board_publications", "boards", "board_id"), [ %w[ board_id boards ] ] ],
        [ "accesses", owned_by("accesses", "boards", "board_id"), [ %w[ board_id boards ], %w[ user_id users ] ] ],

        [ "user_settings", owned_by("user_settings", "users", "user_id"), [ %w[ user_id users ] ] ],
        [ "notification_bundles", owned_by("notification_bundles", "users", "user_id"), [ %w[ user_id users ] ] ],
        [ "notifications", owned_by("notifications", "users", "user_id"), [ %w[ user_id users ], %w[ card_id cards ] ] ],
        [ "push_subscriptions", owned_by("push_subscriptions", "users", "user_id"), [ %w[ user_id users ] ] ],
        [ "search_queries", owned_by("search_queries", "users", "user_id"), [ %w[ user_id users ] ] ],

        [ "comments", owned_by("comments", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ], %w[ creator_id users ] ] ],
        [ "steps", owned_by("steps", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ] ] ],
        [ "assignments", owned_by("assignments", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ], %w[ assignee_id users ], %w[ assigner_id users ] ] ],
        [ "taggings", owned_by("taggings", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ], %w[ tag_id tags ] ] ],
        [ "closures", owned_by("closures", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ] ] ],
        [ "card_goldnesses", owned_by("card_goldnesses", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ] ] ],
        [ "card_not_nows", owned_by("card_not_nows", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ] ] ],
        [ "card_activity_spikes", owned_by("card_activity_spikes", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ] ] ],
        [ "watches", owned_by("watches", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ], %w[ user_id users ] ] ],
        [ "pins", owned_by("pins", "cards", "card_id"), [ %w[ card_id cards ], %w[ user_id users ] ] ],
        [ "mentions", owned_by_polymorphic("mentions", "source", CARD_OR_COMMENT), [ %w[ mentionee_id users ], %w[ mentioner_id users ] ] ],
        [ "reactions", owned_by_polymorphic("reactions", "reactable", CARD_OR_COMMENT), [ %w[ reacter_id users ] ] ],

        [ "webhook_delinquency_trackers", owned_by("webhook_delinquency_trackers", "webhooks", "webhook_id"), [ %w[ webhook_id webhooks ] ] ],
        [ "webhook_deliveries", owned_by("webhook_deliveries", "webhooks", "webhook_id"), [ %w[ webhook_id webhooks ], %w[ event_id events ] ] ],

        [ "action_text_rich_texts", owned_by_polymorphic("action_text_rich_texts", "record", RICH_TEXT_OWNERS), [] ],
        [ "active_storage_attachments", owned_by_polymorphic("active_storage_attachments", "record", ATTACHMENT_OWNERS), [ %w[ blob_id active_storage_blobs ] ] ],
        [ "active_storage_blobs", "(SELECT MIN(active_storage_attachments.account_id) FROM active_storage_attachments WHERE active_storage_attachments.blob_id = active_storage_blobs.id)", [] ],
        [ "active_storage_variant_records", owned_by("active_storage_variant_records", "active_storage_blobs", "blob_id"), [ %w[ blob_id active_storage_blobs ] ] ],

        [ "filters_tags", owned_by("filters_tags", "filters", "filter_id"), [ %w[ filter_id filters ], %w[ tag_id tags ] ] ],
        [ "boards_filters", owned_by("boards_filters", "filters", "filter_id"), [ %w[ filter_id filters ], %w[ board_id boards ] ] ],
        [ "assignees_filters", owned_by("assignees_filters", "filters", "filter_id"), [ %w[ filter_id filters ], %w[ assignee_id users ] ] ],
        [ "creators_filters", owned_by("creators_filters", "filters", "filter_id"), [ %w[ filter_id filters ], %w[ creator_id users ] ] ],
        [ "closers_filters", owned_by("closers_filters", "filters", "filter_id"), [ %w[ filter_id filters ], %w[ closer_id users ] ] ],
        [ "assigners_filters", owned_by("assigners_filters", "filters", "filter_id"), [ %w[ filter_id filters ], %w[ assigner_id users ] ] ]
      ]
    end

    ACCOUNT_OR_BOARD = { "Account" => %w[ accounts id ], "Board" => %w[ boards account_id ] }.freeze
    CARD_OR_COMMENT = { "Card" => %w[ cards account_id ], "Comment" => %w[ comments account_id ] }.freeze
    RICH_TEXT_OWNERS = { "Card" => %w[ cards account_id ], "Comment" => %w[ comments account_id ], "Board" => %w[ boards account_id ] }.freeze
    ATTACHMENT_OWNERS = RICH_TEXT_OWNERS.merge(
      "User" => %w[ users account_id ],
      "Export" => %w[ exports account_id ],
      "Account::Import" => %w[ account_imports account_id ],
      "ActionText::RichText" => %w[ action_text_rich_texts account_id ]
    ).freeze

    def owned_by(table, parent, key)
      "(SELECT #{parent}.account_id FROM #{parent} WHERE #{parent}.id = #{table}.#{key})"
    end

    def owned_by_polymorphic(table, name, owners)
      branches = owners.map do |type, (owner_table, owner_column)|
        "WHEN '#{type}' THEN (SELECT #{owner_table}.#{owner_column} FROM #{owner_table} WHERE #{owner_table}.id = #{table}.#{name}_id)"
      end

      "CASE #{table}.#{name}_type #{branches.join(" ")} END"
    end

    def prune_sql(table, requires)
      conditions = [
        "#{table}.account_id IS NULL",
        "#{table}.account_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM accounts)"
      ]

      requires.each do |column, target|
        conditions << "#{table}.#{column} NOT IN (SELECT id FROM #{target})"
      end

      "DELETE FROM #{table} WHERE #{conditions.join(" OR ")}"
    end

    def leading_account_index?(table)
      indexes(table).any? { |index| index.columns.first == "account_id" }
    end
end
EOF

require "digest"

def bin(label) = CONN.quote(UUIDT.serialize(det(label)))

$fail = 0
def check(desc, sql, expected_rows)
  got = CONN.select_value(sql).to_i
  ok = got == expected_rows
  $fail += 1 unless ok
  puts "#{ok ? 'ok  ' : 'FAIL'} #{desc} (rows=#{got}, expected=#{expected_rows})"
end

# row kept with the expected account
def kept(table, label, account_label)
  sql = "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{table} WHERE id = #{bin(label)} AND account_id = #{bin(account_label)}"
  [ "#{table}:#{label} -> #{account_label}", sql, 1 ]
end
# row must be gone
def dropped(table, label)
  [ "#{table}:#{label} dropped", "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{table} WHERE id = #{bin(label)}", 0 ]
end

checks = []
# users
checks << kept("users", :u1, :a1) << kept("users", :u2, :a2) << dropped("users", :u_null) << dropped("users", :u_dangling)
# tags, join codes, imports

checks << kept("notification_bundles", :nb1, :a1)
checks << kept("push_subscriptions", :ps1, :a1)

check("creators_filters -> a1", "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM creators_filters WHERE account_id=#{bin(:a1)}", 1)
check("closers_filters -> a1", "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM closers_filters WHERE account_id=#{bin(:a1)}", 1)

# every row left in a tenant table has an existing account
%w[users tags account_join_codes boards columns cards filters webhooks events entropies storage_totals board_publications accesses user_settings notification_bundles notifications push_subscriptions search_queries comments steps assignments taggings closures card_goldnesses card_not_nows card_activity_spikes watches pins mentions reactions webhook_delinquency_trackers webhook_deliveries action_text_rich_texts active_storage_attachments active_storage_blobs active_storage_variant_records filters_tags boards_filters assignees_filters creators_filters closers_filters assigners_filters].each do |t|
  check("#{t}: no NULL or dangling account_id", "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM #{t} WHERE account_id IS NULL OR account_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM accounts)", 0)
end

# schema: NOT NULL and an index led by account_id, on every tenant table
%w[users tags account_join_codes account_imports boards columns cards filters webhooks events entropies storage_totals board_publications accesses user_settings notification_bundles notifications push_subscriptions search_queries comments steps assignments taggings closures card_goldnesses card_not_nows card_activity_spikes watches pins mentions reactions webhook_delinquency_trackers webhook_deliveries action_text_rich_texts active_storage_attachments active_storage_blobs active_storage_variant_records filters_tags boards_filters assignees_filters creators_filters closers_filters assigners_filters].each do |t|
  col = CONN.columns(t).find { |c| c.name == "account_id" }
  notnull = col && !col.null
  leading = CONN.indexes(t).any? { |i| i.columns.first == "account_id" }
  unless notnull && leading
    $fail += 1
    puts "FAIL schema #{t}: notnull=#{notnull.inspect} leading_index=#{leading}"
  end
end
puts "schema NOT NULL + leading index check done"
puts($fail.zero? ? "ALL CHECKS PASSED" : "#{$fail} FAILURES")
EOF

def blocks(path)
  out = {}; cur = nil
  File.readlines(path).each do |l|
    if (m = l.match(/^\s*create_table "([^"]+)"/)) then cur = m[1]; out[cur] = []
    elsif cur && l =~ /^\s*end\s*$/ then cur = nil
    elsif cur then out[cur] << l.strip.sub(/, charset.*$/, "").sub(/, collation.*$/, "")
    end
  end
  out
end

a.each do |t, lines|
  next unless b[t]
  only_a = lines - b[t]; only_b = b[t] - lines
  puts "#{t}: only-in-mysql=#{only_a.inspect} only-in-sqlite=#{only_b.inspect}" if only_a.any? || only_b.any?
end

messages.content: The two dumps differ in string limits and MySQL-only index options, but the `account_id` lines are identical. I'll derive the MySQL `schema.rb` edits from the SQLite dump, touching only `account_id` columns and their indexes, and then check that the column and index order matches the SQLite dump for every table. Next I'll sync the new `schema_sqlite.rb` from the migrated scratch copy.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cp /tmp/work/mig/db/schema_sqlite.rb db/schema_sqlite.rb && git diff --stat -- db/ && cat > /tmp/work/mysql_schema_patch.rb <<'EOF'
# Applies the account_id changes from the (new) SQLite dump to the MySQL schema.rb, touching
# only account_id columns and their indexes. Usage: ruby mysql_schema_patch.rb orig_sqlite new_sqlite mysql_in mysql_out
def table_blocks(path)
  blocks = {}; cur = nil
  File.readlines(path).each do |l|
    if (m = l.match(/^  create_table "([^"]+)"/)) then cur = m[1]; blocks[cur] = []
    elsif cur && l =~ /^  end\s*$/ then blocks[cur] << l; cur = nil
    elsif cur then blocks[cur] << l
    end
  end
  blocks
end

def column_name(line) = line[/^\s*t\.(?!index\b)\w+ "([^"]+)"/, 1]
def index_name(line) = line[/^\s*t\.index .*name: "([^"]+)"/, 1]

orig_sqlite, new_sqlite, mysql_in, mysql_out = ARGV
old_s = table_blocks(orig_sqlite)
new_s = table_blocks(new_sqlite)
lines = File.readlines(mysql_in)
mysql = table_blocks(mysql_in)

# Rebuild the file as a list of [table, blockLines] segments, editing only changed tables.
out = []
i = 0
while i < lines.size
  l = lines[i]
  if (m = l.match(/^  create_table "([^"]+)"/))
    table = m[1]
    block_end = i
    block_end += 1 until lines[block_end] =~ /^  end\s*$/
    body = lines[(i + 1)...block_end]
    if new_s.key?(table) && old_s.key?(table)
      nb = new_s[table]; ob = old_s[table]
      acct_old = ob.find { |x| column_name(x) == "account_id" }
      acct_new = nb.find { |x| column_name(x) == "account_id" }
      if acct_old && acct_new && acct_old != acct_new
        body = body.map { |x| column_name(x) == "account_id" ? acct_new.sub(/\A\s*/, "    ").then { |s| x[/\A\s*/] + s.strip + "\n" } : x }
      end
      if acct_new && !acct_old
        # insert the column in sorted position among the existing column lines
        col_idx = body.index { |x| (n = column_name(x)) && n > "account_id" }
        if col_idx
          body.insert(col_idx, "    #{acct_new.strip}\n")
        else
          last_col = body.rindex { |x| column_name(x) }
          body.insert(last_col + 1, "    #{acct_new.strip}\n")
        end
      end
      # indexes that exist only in the new dump
      new_idx_names = nb.map { |x| index_name(x) }.compact
      old_idx_names = ob.map { |x| index_name(x) }.compact
      (new_idx_names - old_idx_names).each do |name|
        new_line = nb.find { |x| index_name(x) == name }
        pos = new_idx_names.index(name)
        prev_name = pos > 0 ? new_idx_names[pos - 1] : nil
        if prev_name
          at = body.index { |x| index_name(x) == prev_name } + 1
        else
          at = body.index { |x| index_name(x) } || body.size
        end
        body.insert(at, new_line.end_with?("\n") ? new_line : "#{new_line}\n")
      end
    end
    out << l
    out.concat(body)
    out << lines[block_end]
    i = block_end + 1
    next
  end
  out << l
  i += 1
end
File.write(mysql_out, out.join)
puts "wrote #{mysql_out}"
EOF

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > /tmp/work/check_mysql.rb <<'EOF'
load "/tmp/work/mysql_schema_patch.rb" if false
def table_blocks(path)
  blocks = {}; cur = nil
  File.readlines(path).each do |l|
    if (m = l.match(/^  create_table "([^"]+)"/)) then cur = m[1]; blocks[cur] = []
    elsif cur && l =~ /^  end\s*$/ then cur = nil
    elsif cur then blocks[cur] << l
    end
  end
  blocks
end
def cols(b) = b.map { |x| x[/^\s*t\.(?!index\b)\w+ "([^"]+)"/, 1] }.compact
def idx(b) = b.map { |x| x[/^\s*t\.index .*name: "([^"]+)"/, 1] }.compact
def acct(b) = b.find { |x| x[/^\s*t\.(?!index\b)\w+ "account_id"/] }&.include?("null: false")
mysql = table_blocks(ARGV[0]); sqlite = table_blocks(ARGV[1])
bad = 0
sqlite.each do |t, sb|
  next if t.start_with?("search_records")
  mb = mysql[t] or (puts "missing table in mysql: #{t}"; bad += 1; next)
  if cols(mb) != cols(sb) then puts "column order differs: #{t}\n  mysql #{cols(mb)}\n  sqlite #{cols(sb)}"; bad += 1 end
  if idx(mb) != idx(sb) then puts "index order differs: #{t}\n  mysql #{idx(mb)}\n  sqlite #{idx(sb)}"; bad += 1 end
  if (sb.any? { |x| x.include?('"account_id"') }) && acct(mb) != acct(sb) then puts "account_id nullability differs: #{t}"; bad += 1 end
end
puts bad.zero? ? "MySQL schema matches SQLite dump for account_id columns, index & column order" : "#{bad} problems"
EOF

cd /app && cat > /tmp/work/fixture_accounts.rb <<'EOF'
require "yaml"

# Table each fixture file loads into (nested dirs map to underscored names, e.g. card/goldnesses -> card_goldnesses).
def table_for(path) = path.delete_suffix(".yml").tr("/", "_")

FILES = Dir["test/fixtures/**/*.yml"].sort
TABLE_OF = FILES.to_h { |f| [ f, table_for(f.delete_prefix("test/fixtures/")) ] }

# Reference attribute -> table holding the referenced label (polymorphic handled separately).
REF_TABLE = {
  "board" => "boards", "card" => "cards", "user" => "users", "creator" => "users",
  "comment" => "comments", "webhook" => "webhooks", "event" => "events", "tag" => "tags",
  "filter" => "filters", "mentioner" => "users", "mentionee" => "users", "assigner" => "users",
  "assignee" => "users", "reacter" => "users", "account" => "accounts"
}
POLY_TYPE_TABLE = { "Card" => "cards", "Comment" => "comments", "Board" => "boards", "Account" => "accounts" }
POLY_ATTRS = %w[ record source container eventable reactable ]

index = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = {} }
FILES.each do |f|
  text = File.read(f).gsub(/<%=.*?%>/m, "X")  # ERB only affects ids and timestamps here
  data = YAML.safe_load(text, aliases: true) || {}
  data.each { |label, attrs| index[TABLE_OF[f]][label.to_s] = attrs }
end

def strip(label) = label.to_s.sub(/\s*\(.*\)\s*\z/, "").delete_suffix("_uuid")

def account_for(index, table, label, seen = [])
  return nil if seen.include?([ table, label ])
  row = index[table][label]
  return nil unless row
  return strip(row["account"]) if row.key?("account")

  row.each do |attr, value|
    if REF_TABLE.key?(attr) && attr != "account"
      found = account_for(index, REF_TABLE[attr], strip(value), seen + [ [ table, label ] ])
      return found if found
    elsif POLY_ATTRS.include?(attr)
      type = value.to_s[/\((\w+)\)\s*\z/, 1]
      target = POLY_TYPE_TABLE[type]
      next unless target
      if target == "accounts"
        return strip(value)
      end
      found = account_for(index, target, strip(value), seen + [ [ table, label ] ])
      return found if found
    end
  end
  nil
end

FILES.each do |f|
  table = TABLE_OF[f]
  next if %w[identities sessions magic_links identity_access_tokens accounts account_external_id_sequences action_pack_passkeys].include?(table)
  next if table == "identity_access_tokens"
  index[table].each do |label, attrs|
    next if attrs.is_a?(Hash) && attrs.key?("account")
    account = account_for(index, table, label)
    plan[f] ||= []
    plan[f] << [ label, account ]
  end
end

plan.each do |f, rows|
  puts "#{f}"
  rows.each { |label, account| puts "   #{label} -> #{account.inspect}" }
end

messages.content: Rails needs the through association declared before the `has-many-through` that uses it. There's also an ordering hazard: `dependent: :delete_all` runs as a before-destroy callback, so `remove_from_filters` has to be registered before it. I'll move the selection association into `Filterable`, derive the join class from the model name, and register the callback first. That removes the duplicate declarations from `Tag` and `Board`.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/concerns/filterable.rb <<'EOF'
module Filterable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    # Declared before the selections so this runs before they're deleted with the record.
    before_destroy :remove_from_filters

    has_many :filter_selections, class_name: "Filter::#{name}Selection", dependent: :delete_all
    has_many :filters, through: :filter_selections

    after_update { filters.touch_all }
  end

  private
    # FIXME: This is too inefficient to have part of a destroy transaction.
    # Need to find a way to use a job or a single query.
    def remove_from_filters
      filters.each { it.resource_removed self }
    end
end
EOF
perl -0pi -e 's/  has_many :filter_selections, class_name: "Filter::TagSelection", dependent: :delete_all\n//' app/models/tag.rb && perl -0pi -e 's/  has_many :filter_selections, class_name: "Filter::BoardSelection", dependent: :delete_all\n//' app/models/board.rb && git diff -- app/models/tag.rb app/models/board.rb app/models/concerns/filterable.rb

require "test_helper"

class Account::TenantTablesTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  # Tables that hold no account's data: the tenant root, identity and authentication records,
  # and Rails internals. Every other table must be tenant-scoped.
  GLOBAL_TABLES = %w[
    accounts account_external_id_sequences action_pack_passkeys ar_internal_metadata
    identities identity_access_tokens magic_links schema_migrations sessions
  ]

  test "every tenant table requires an indexed account_id" do
    connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection

    (connection.tables - GLOBAL_TABLES).each do |table|
      column = connection.columns(table).find { |c| c.name == "account_id" }
      assert column, "#{table} has no account_id"
      assert_not column.null, "#{table}.account_id must be NOT NULL"
      assert connection.indexes(table).any? { |index| index.columns.first == "account_id" }, "#{table}.account_id must be indexed"
    end
  end
end

I'll exclude them in the test with a comment saying why, so the test passes in both modes. I can't run SaaS mode here, so I'll say so in my summary.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > test/models/account/tenant_tables_test.rb <<'EOF'
require "test_helper"

class Account::TenantTablesTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  # Tables that hold no account's data: the tenant root, identity and session records, and
  # infrastructure. Every other table must be tenant-scoped.
  GLOBAL_TABLES = %w[
    accounts account_external_id_sequences action_pack_passkeys action_push_native_devices
    ar_internal_metadata identities identity_access_tokens magic_links schema_migrations sessions
  ]
  GLOBAL_TABLE_PATTERN = /\A(audits|console)1984_/ # SaaS-only admin console and audit logs

  test "every tenant table requires an indexed account_id" do
    connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection

    connection.tables.each do |table|
      next if GLOBAL_TABLES.include?(table) || table.match?(GLOBAL_TABLE_PATTERN)

      column = connection.columns(table).find { |c| c.name == "account_id" }
      assert column, "#{table} has no account_id"
      assert_not column.null, "#{table}.account_id must be NOT NULL"
      assert connection.indexes(table).any? { |index| index.columns.first == "account_id" }, "#{table}.account_id must be indexed"
    end
  end
end
EOF

The rollout is finished, with one migration for the data and one for the tag index. The full suite passes on the final state: 1543 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors, 2 skips. The baseline was 1542 runs with 1 failure and 139 errors. Rubocop and brakeman are clean.

## What changed

**Schema (one data migration, `20260710120000_require_account_id_on_tenant_tables`)**
- Every tenant table now has a NOT NULL, indexed `account_id`. That's 46 tables: 15 core tables that already had the column, plus 31 that gained it. The global tables (`accounts`, `identities`, `sessions`, `magic_links`, `identity_access_tokens`, `action_pack_passkeys`, and the account-ID counter) are unchanged.
- Each `account_id` is backfilled from the row's parent chain, parents first. A row is an orphan if its account can't be resolved, its account no longer exists, or a required reference is gone. Orphans are deleted.
- Blobs take their account from their attachments.
- `down` reverses the DDL. Deleted rows are not restored.
- I tested this on a scratch copy seeded with valid rows and about 40 orphan and edge cases, checking each one, and also tested rollback.

**Tags (`20260710120100_scope_tag_titles_to_account`)**
- The unique index on `tags.title` alone blocked two accounts from both having a `"ruby"` tag. I made it unique per account. This is a call I made beyond the literal request, because the code already scopes tags per account and a test asserts it.

**Models and code**
- About 20 models gained `belongs_to :account, default: -> { parent.account }`, following the existing core-model pattern. Blobs, attachments, rich texts, and variant records got the same through initializers.
- `Search::Query` now takes a user, and `Search::Query.wrap` requires one.
- The eight habtm join tables on filters became explicit join models (`Filter::Selection` and five subclasses), so their rows can carry `account_id`.
- The raw `Access.insert_all` calls now pass `account_id`.
- `Account::Incineratable` called `account.destroy` on an `Account`, which raised `NameError`. It now calls `destroy`.

**Fixtures and schema files**
- Every tenant fixture row got an account. Three `Conversation::Message` rich-text fixtures were removed. That model doesn't exist, the records they point at don't exist either, and they were the orphan case in fixture form.
- `db/schema_sqlite.rb` is generated from the migrated scratch copy.
- `db/schema.rb` (MySQL) had to be hand-derived from that dump, because there's no MySQL server here. A script checked that its column order, index order, and nullability match the SQLite dump.

**New test:** `Account::TenantTablesTest` asserts every table outside an explicit global list has a NOT NULL, indexed `account_id`. It fails on the original schema with 43 tables.

## Caveats
- **MySQL is untested.** The migration uses portable SQL, but I haven't run it against MySQL. It's a full-table pass with correlated subqueries and no batching, so it may be slow on large production tables.
- **SaaS mode was not run.** It needs private gems and MySQL. The new test excludes the SaaS-only admin-console and audit tables by name.
- **Data removed beyond the core orphans:**
  - Identity avatar attachments, since nothing in the app attaches them.
  - Unattached blobs, including any direct upload still in flight at deploy time.
  - The files for deleted blobs stay in the storage service and need a separate purge.
- **Mismatched existing rows are not repaired.** A row whose `account_id` disagrees with its parent's account is kept as it is, because it isn't an orphan.
